tier_reason: Independent third-party measurement in a competing library's repo (hazae41/berith README Node table, code at src/node/bench/index.bench.ts, Apple M1 Max, Node v18.12.1) that shows supercop.wasm 5.0.1 at 187.96 us/iter against @noble/curves 0.7.0 at 1.99 ms/iter; the measured wasm's emcc flags are public in supercop.wasm's gulpfile.ls, but the Emscripten version is unstated and the README table includes serialized rows the current bench file no longer has, so it falls short of A.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: Measured artifact is the prebuilt npm supercop.wasm 5.0.1; its build in gulpfile.ls runs emcc on orlp/ed25519 with -Oz --llvm-lto 1 --closure 1 -s WASM=1 -s NO_EXIT_RUNTIME=1 -s NO_FILESYSTEM=1 (size-optimized; Emscripten version not stated). The benchmark is JavaScript run with Node v18.12.1.
corrections.caveats: Third-party benchmark in a competing library's repository (hazae41/berith, 7 stars, now marked DEPRECATED by its author): public code, CPU and Node version stated, but one machine, 1,000 samples, and a mixed keygen+sign+verify iteration rather than separate operations, so tier B rather than A. The current bench file at HEAD (last changed 2023-10-12) has no serialized node:crypto or serialized berith rows, so the README table came from an earlier version of the harness. The wasm is built with -Oz (size, not speed), and the Emscripten version is unstated. Neither tweetnacl-js nor a native SUPERCOP ed25519 build appears in the table; the JS baseline is @noble/curves 0.7.0, and the native node:crypto row with KeyObject (unserialized) keys beats supercop.wasm (152.67 vs 187.96 us/iter). The serialized node:crypto row (555.61 us/iter) is the closer like-for-like comparison, since supercop.wasm works on raw key bytes. Last commit and last npm release are both 2018-02-24, so the code is old and unmaintained. The licence is listed on GitHub as Free Public License 1.0.0 / Zero Clause BSD (0BSD, OSI-approved, no patent grant).

notes: Numbers match the berith README Node table exactly; ratios in claimed_speedup are correctly marked as derived. Main shortcomings: about 10.6x faster than pure-JS @noble/curves 0.7.0, but slower than native node:crypto with unserialized keys; the benchmark is a single run on an M1 Max by a competitor; the wasm build is size-optimized and the project has been abandoned since 2018. The repo README is readme.md (lowercase) and makes no speed claim.
